Its blow-the-trumpet collocation, תִּקְע֣וּ שׁוֹפָ֔ר (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier), echoes תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) at Jer.4.5 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide, not exclusive), and its closing colon, מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier), is byte-identical to מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) at Jer.4.6, a string standing at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys); the opening imperative itself is a mater-lectionis pair with that same verse, plene הָעִ֖יזוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) at Jer.4.6 against defective הָעִ֣זוּ (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier) here, each spelling standing at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each, MT keys). The summons runs through the siege description at Jer.6.2-Jer.6.3 (shepherds pitching tents against the daughter of Zion) without a further imperative or vocative address, before the besiegers' own quoted battle-cry at Jer.6.4.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the siege description (Jer.6.2-Jer.6.3) from the opening summons: Jer.6.2 turns to first person, דָּמִ֖יתִי (oshb:Jer.6.2, byte tier), while Jer.6.3 is third person, and neither carries an imperative, a vocative or a speech formula, so no tier-1 onset separates them from the summons.
